item.title: Supreme Court Directs Medical Care for Injured Jantar Mantar Protestors
item.description: The Supreme Court of India has directed that proper medical treatment be provided to protestors who sustained pellet gun injuries during a demonstration at Jantar Mantar. The apex court also asked the Central Government to preserve the ammunition log of the Rapid Action Force used during the protest led by CJP. While hearing a plea seeking a total ban on pellet guns, the court questioned how pellets could be prohibited when bullets remain permissible in extreme circumstances. Meanwhile, amid the ongoing row, the CRPF chief urged personnel to execute their duties fearlessly.

item.title: IIT Bombay Alumnus Jagdish Aphale Appointed Secretary of Ram Temple Trust
item.description: The Ayodhya Ram Temple trust has appointed Jagdish Aphale, an IIT Bombay alumnus and RSS leader, as its secretary to oversee temple management. This key appointment follows recent reports regarding an alleged donation theft controversy surrounding the temple's funds. Aphale steps into the role as the trust's first secretary designated to handle administrative responsibilities. Further operational details regarding his specific plans or official duties remain limited in the available context, but his selection comes amid efforts to manage temple administration effectively following the recent donation row.

item.title: CWG 2026: Neeraj Chopra Begins Javelin Campaign; Toor Eyes Medal
item.description: Indian track and field athletes take centre stage at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow on July 30, marking Day 8 of the competition. Star javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra is set to begin his campaign to reclaim the javelin title and target his second Commonwealth Games gold medal, despite facing a transformed competitive field. Additionally, shot putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor will feature in his discipline, aiming to secure a medal for the country. India looks to add more medals to its tally as the full event schedule unfolds throughout the day.

item.title: SC asks Centre to preserve RAF ammunition logs from Jantar Mantar protest
item.description: The Supreme Court of India has directed the Central government to preserve records and logs of Rapid Action Force ammunition deployed during a protest at Jantar Mantar organised by Citizens for Justice and Peace. While considering a plea seeking a ban on pellet guns, the apex court indicated that such weapons may be used in exceptional circumstances and announced plans to examine existing crowd control protocols. Additionally, the court directed the Delhi government to guarantee proper medical treatment for injured protesters. This development comes as medical experts warn that pellet gun injuries can result in irreversible damage and permanent disability.

item.title: Kharge Questions Anti-Paper Leak Bill In Parliament Monsoon Session
item.description: During the Parliament Monsoon Session 2026, Leader Mallikarjun Kharge questioned the effectiveness of the anti-paper leak legislation, calling government amendments a hogwash while supporting NEET protesters. The Bharatiya Janata Party criticized Kharge over his remarks concerning Home Minister Amit Shah. Meanwhile, parliamentary proceedings faced disruptions, and the Rajya Sabha was adjourned twice as opposition members demanded the presence of the Home Minister to address protest crackdowns, reflecting heightened political tensions in the House.

item.title: Shell Profits Double as Oil Prices Rise Amid Strait of Hormuz Disruptions
item.description: Shell has recorded a doubling of its profits following a notable increase in international energy prices. This rise in market rates is linked to conflict involving Iran, which has caused significant disruptions to global supply chains. In particular, shipments of crude oil and liquid natural gas passing through the vital Strait of Hormuz have been severely impacted. Consequently, restricted global supply has led to higher energy costs worldwide.
